title: Best Affirmation Apps 2026: ThinkUp, I Am, Innertune
description: The best affirmation apps in 2026, compared by how they work — your own recorded voice, ready-made professional audio, or text on your lock screen: ThinkUp, I am, Innertune, Mantra, Manifestive, manifestlings and Anicca, verified against App Store listings read in November 2026.
markdown:
By Anicca · November 2026

The best affirmation app depends on how you want to hear your lines: in your own recorded voice (ThinkUp, Mantra), as ready-made professional audio (Innertune), or as text on your lock screen (I am). This page compares them by how they work, using store pages checked in November 2026. If you only want the short answer: ThinkUp is the one you record, Innertune is the one you listen to, I am is the one you read, and Anicca (our app) is the text option built around a new affirmation on your Lock Screen every day. For the longer eleven-app comparison with the same store-checked method, see our [full guide to the best affirmation apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-2026-11-05), and for iPhone only, our [guide to the best affirmation apps for iPhone](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-for-iphone-2026-11-12).

*Disclosure: Anicca is our own app; it is listed among the options below, and no app paid to be here. Prices and ratings come from each app's US App Store listing, read in November 2026; where a price was unclear on the listing, we say "see the store page" instead of guessing.*

## Three ways an affirmation app can work

Most affirmation apps look alike in the store, with a soft gradient, a stream of "I am" lines and a subscription screen. Underneath, they split into three designs, and the design matters more than the feature list.

The first is your own voice. You write or pick a line, record yourself saying it, and the app plays it back on a loop, often over music. The second is ready-made audio: a professional voice reads a large library of affirmations for you, usually with background sound. The third is text: a short line arrives on your lock screen or in a widget, and you read it in your head.

Research on affirmations is mixed enough that the design is worth thinking about. A well-known 2009 study in Psychological Science (Wood, Perunovic and Lee) found that repeating positive self-statements lifted mood for people who already felt good about themselves, and made people with low self-esteem feel slightly worse. Brain-imaging work by Cascio and colleagues in 2016 found that affirming your own values activated regions linked to self-related thinking and reward. Neither result promises anything about your life. Both suggest the same practical rule: the line has to be one you can half-believe, and it helps when it sounds like you.

That is why the comparison below starts with how each app delivers the line, not with how many lines it holds.

## ThinkUp: your own voice, on repeat

ThinkUp is the clearest example of the own-voice design. On its App Store page, the developer (Precise Wellness LLC) describes recording affirmations in your own voice, choosing background music, and scheduling notifications and auto-play loops. The listing also describes a curated library of 300+ affirmations across 10+ life goals, personal images for your affirmation cards, Apple Health tracking of mindful minutes, and Apple Watch support.

Its App Store rating was 4.7 from about 7,500 ratings when we checked in November 2026. The app runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch, and there is a Google Play listing as well. It is the only app on this page with clean, single prices published on its US listing: $7.99 a month, $39.99 a year, or $99.99 for lifetime access.

The strength is intimacy. Hearing your own steady voice say a line at bedtime feels different from hearing a stranger say it, and many people find that the recording step forces them to choose words they can actually say out loud. The trade-off is effort: you have to do the recording, and the built-in library is much smaller than the giant audio catalogs elsewhere.

## I am: text first, on your lock screen

I am, from Monkey Taps, sits at the text end of the range. Its store listing describes lock screen affirmations that change daily, home screen widgets, Apple Watch reminders, custom notification times, a favourites list, focus categories such as self-esteem and confidence, and regularly updated themes. It has a very large rating base, 4.8 from 738,672 US ratings when we checked in November 2026, and it is available on Android too.

There is no audio-first mode here, so it works best for people who like a quick line between other things: a widget you glance at, a notification at noon. That makes it the lightest option on this page, and the easiest habit to keep going on a busy day. If you want a voice, music or a longer session, it is not built for that. Premium is $60 a year, $15 a month or $150 lifetime on the US listing, sold monthly, yearly and as a lifetime purchase; see the store page for current prices in your country.

## Innertune: a huge audio library, plus your voice

Innertune, made by Innertune Media Inc., takes the ready-made audio route and adds the own-voice option on top. Its store listing describes about 77,000 affirmations across 550+ playlists, 19 voices plus an ASMR option, 100+ binaural beat tracks, a night mode for sleep, daily reminders, personalised 21-day plans, streaks, and recording in your own voice over background music. Offline downloads come with premium. The App Store rating was 4.8 from about 12,000 ratings when we checked, and it runs on iPhone and Android. Premium is $29.99 a year on the US listing.

This is the broadest of the three, and the one to try if you want to press play and be guided rather than build your own set. The catch is the same as with any big library: choosing takes time, and a subscription is required for the full feature set. There is a free trial, and plans are weekly, monthly and yearly; see the store page for the current numbers in your country.

## Two more worth a look: Mantra and Manifestive

**Mantra** is an iOS-first app with 1,000+ "I am" affirmations across 30+ categories, own-voice recording, smart daytime and bedtime reminders and customisable themes, at a 4.8 rating from about 34,000 ratings when the manifestlings comparison checked store pages in September 2026. It is a good middle path between I am and ThinkUp. It is sold as weekly, monthly, three-month, annual and lifetime options, so check the store page before you commit.

**Manifestive** is closer to a manifestation toolbox than a pure affirmation player: affirmations, guided visualisation, a journal, mood tracking, a vision board builder and voice affirmation recording, on iOS and Android, with a free tier and paid weekly and monthly plans ($1.99 a week or $8.99 a month, as listed in the manifestlings manifestation roundup). If you are still deciding what kind of practice you want, a toolbox like this lets you try several in one place.

## How to choose

Start with one honest question: what have you actually stuck with before? If you never open apps but always see your lock screen, I am or Anicca fits. If you like to lie down and listen, Innertune fits. If the thing that would make you believe a line is hearing it in your own voice, ThinkUp or Mantra fits.

Then think about the line itself. Keep it short, present tense and something you can say without wincing. "I am learning to trust myself" tends to hold up better than "I am completely confident" on a wobbly day. That follows directly from the 2009 result above: a line too far from what you believe can work against you, whichever app delivers it.

Finally, remember that an app is a container. Nothing here promises a result, and a good app only makes it easier to show up. If a subscription makes you feel pressured, the free tiers are worth a full week before you pay.

## Pricing, checked November 2026

Only ThinkUp published clean, single prices on the US App Store page when we checked: $7.99 a month, $39.99 a year and $99.99 for life. I am lists $60 a year, Innertune $29.99 a year, and Anicca Premium is $59.99 a year on the US listing. For every other app on this page, the store lists several plans or ranges, so we point you to the store page instead of quoting a number that might be wrong by the time you read this. Prices also differ by country and change without notice.

Two habits save money. Read the auto-renew terms on the paywall before you tap, and set a calendar reminder for the day a trial ends. And if you plan to stay, compare the yearly price with twelve months of the monthly one; the gap is often large.

## Questions people ask

**Which affirmation app lets me record my own voice?**

ThinkUp, Innertune, Mantra and Manifestive all offer own-voice recording, according to their store listings in November 2026. ThinkUp is built around it, while Innertune adds it to a large ready-made audio library. I am and Anicca do not offer recording; they are text apps.

**Are affirmation apps free?**

Most can be downloaded without paying up front, and several keep a limited free tier. The full features, such as offline downloads or the biggest libraries, sit behind a subscription. ThinkUp lists $7.99 a month, $39.99 a year and $99.99 lifetime; for the others, see the store page.

**Do affirmations actually work?**

The evidence is mixed. Studies suggest affirmations can help people who already feel reasonably secure, and can backfire for people with low self-esteem when the lines are too far from what they believe (Wood, Perunovic and Lee, 2009). Choose lines you can half-believe, treat an app as a way to keep a habit, and expect no promised result.

**Is there an affirmation app with a virtual pet?**

Not among the audio and text players above. manifestlings is built around a virtual pet (a dreamling) that grows on what you practise, and it is on the App Store for iPhone and on Google Play for Android.
